answer: Each new agent streams 4096 timestamps, sealed under a ChaCha20-Poly1305 cipher, to a bridge relayer over 72 hours. The relayer regresses arrival times against the agent's own counter, extracting the quartz oscillator skew to 0.05 ppm. A registry rejects any identity whose skew sits within 0.2 ppm of an existing one, so admission needs genuinely distinct crystals. Faking 10,000 identities means buying 10,000 boards at about $35, or $350,000, plus 720,000 board-hours of burn-in. Cloud VMs collide. Crystal tolerances behave like fingerprints pressed into wet cement, one per board.
